steps.title: A second shape: doing it with someone
body: You've already met Form II's doubled middle consonant (دَرَسَ → دَرَّسَ). Form III marks itself differently: a long alif after the *first* root consonant instead — وَزْن فَاعَلَ. Where Form II often means "cause [someone] to do X," Form III most often means "do X toward or together with someone" — a reciprocal or associative sense.

كَتَبَ ("he wrote") becomes كَاتَبَ ("he corresponded with someone" — writing back and forth). جَلَسَ ("he sat") becomes جَالَسَ ("he sat together with someone," kept them company). The root and its core meaning stay exactly the same; only the relationship to another person changes.

Form III can also be denominative, exactly like Form II can — صَدِيق ("friend") becomes صَادَقَ ("he befriended someone"), with no Form I verb behind it at all. And you already know one Form III verb from A2 without realising it: سَافَرَ ("to travel") — a reminder that this pattern doesn't always need a Form I partner to make sense. The present tense keeps the long alif and adds يُـ: يُكَاتِبُ, يُجَالِسُ, يُصَادِقُ, يُسَافِرُ.

steps.title: Form III in four sentences
steps.intro: Read each sentence, then compare the Form III verb to the Form I or noun it's built from. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: Doubled consonant or long alif?
steps.prompt: Which pattern marks Form III — reciprocal, "toward or with someone"?

options.label: كَاتَبَ (kātaba) — long alif after the first consonant
دَرَّسَ (darrasa) — doubled middle consonant, that's Form II

steps.explanation: Form III's signature is the long alif right after the first root consonant (فَاعَلَ) — visually distinct from Form II's doubled middle consonant (فَعَّلَ), even though both often sit on the same root family of meanings.

steps.title: Reciprocal: sit → sit together with
steps.prompt: جَلَسَ means "he sat." What does the Form III جَالَسَ mean?

options.label: He sat together with someone / kept them company

steps.explanation: Form III's reciprocal/associative sense turns a plain action into one shared with another person — "he sat" becomes "he sat together with [someone]." كَاتَبَ ("to correspond with," from كَتَبَ) works the same way.

steps.title: Denominative: friend → to befriend
steps.prompt: صَدِيق is the noun "friend." What does the Form III verb صَادَقَ mean?

options.label: To befriend / take someone as a friend
To be a friend (a state, not an action)

steps.explanation: صَادَقَ is denominative, built straight from صَدِيق — the same way نَظَّفَ was built from نَظِيف back in Form II. سَافَرَ ("to travel"), which you already knew from A2, is also Form III, though its own Form I partner isn't part of this course.

steps.title: Two derived forms down, eight to go
steps.message: Form II's causative/denominative doubling and Form III's reciprocal/associative long alif — four more worked examples: كَاتَبَ, جَالَسَ, صَادَقَ, and سَافَرَ. Forms IV–X are still ahead.
